children: Expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in October surged past 70% Wednesday on the back of hawkish central bank commentary and a fresh wave of inflationary pressures that pushed Treasury yields to new multi-year highs.

Federal funds futures traders now price in a 70.9% probability that the Fed will raise its benchmark overnight rate by 25 basis points to a range of 4.00% to 4.25% at its Oct. 28 meeting, up from a 55.4% chance just a day ago.

Market participants are also bracing for the possibility of even more tightening before the year is out. Additional futures data from CME Group indicates a 55.7% chance that the target rate will climb a full 50 basis points higher to the 425 to 450 basis point range by the Dec. 9 meeting.
The repricing comes on the heels of the Fed’s decision last week to hike rates in response to persistently elevated inflation readings fueled by rising energy prices.
